author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Organize multidisc PS2 games without losing disc order or region
summary: Verify each owned disc independently, record serial and hash relationships, adopt explicit Disc 1/Disc 2 names, test the game's real swap or save handoff, and roll back the complete set together.
heroAlt: K3b optical-disc image panel used to identify and preserve one disc at a time in a multidisc set

blocks.text: Prove membership before naming a set

A multidisc release is a relationship among separate physical discs, not one oversized image. Each disc must retain its own dump log, hash, serial or volume evidence, region, and order. Some games request a live disc change; others write a transfer save and ask for the next disc after a reboot. The organization must follow the game's real handoff rather than an assumed playlist feature.
Do not concatenate images, rename two unrelated regional discs into one set, or patch a preservation master to simplify switching. Keep each verified disc image intact.

items: Every personally owned disc dumped and verified separately.
SHA-256, byte size, region, and label recorded for each image.
The game's manual or an observed legal playthrough identifying the handoff method.
A backup of the memory card used for the transition test.
An unambiguous base title and explicit disc-number convention.

blocks.text: Name, scan, and exercise the actual handoff

items: 1. Create one folder for the set and place only its verified working images inside.
2. Name every image with the same base title, region, and explicit Disc number while preserving its extension and cue/bin relationships.
3. Add the parent set folder through the existing non-overlapping library root; do not select each disc folder as another root.
4. Refresh once and verify that EmuCoreX shows separate entries or disc identities without collapsing a regional variant.
5. Cold-boot Disc 1, make a native in-game save before the handoff, and close normally.
6. Follow the title's documented swap or save-transfer method with Disc 2; never force a state captured under the wrong disc.
7. Restart from the memory card and prove the transition works without relying on an emulator state.

blocks.text: A matching marketing title does not prove that two images belong together. PAL, NTSC-U, NTSC-J, demo, bonus, and revision discs may use different executables or save expectations. Store the disc-set manifest beside private backup documentation, not inside a scanned folder if the app might index it.
The set is ready when identity, ordering, and native progress transfer all agree.

items: Every disc hash matches its independent dump record.
Names expose region and disc order without relying on sort punctuation.
Disc 1 and Disc 2 cold-boot as their intended identities.
The game's real handoff accepts the next disc or its transfer save.
Progress remains visible after a full restart from the memory card.
Next disc rejects the save: region or revision may not match the first disc.
Music disappears on one disc: its cue/bin tracks are incomplete.
The same cover hides both entries: compare paths and serials before removing anything.
A save state loads only with the original disc: return to a native save at the transition point.

blocks.text: Remove the set from the active root, restore every image and cue/bin component from the verified working backup, and restore the pre-test memory card. Reintroduce Disc 1 alone, prove its identity, then add the remaining discs only after the manifest has been corrected.
Do not promise automatic disc switching

Front ends and emulator builds differ in how they expose disc changes. The durable method is the one the original game supports through its own save or prompt. Document the observed EmuCoreX flow for the current build instead of assuming a desktop playlist feature exists on Android.
